prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create a polished, modelable concept-art review board for Deep Frontier, a Timberborn Iron Teeth mod. It must look like an authentic extension of Timberborn's Iron Teeth art direction: chunky stylized low-poly architecture, thick squared dark timber, weathered warm planks, angular charcoal iron bands with visible large rivets, restrained dark green/oxidized metal roofs, practical exposed mechanical assemblies, soft painted textures, warm daylight, game-camera orthographic isometric view. Deliberately designed recognizable buildings, credible joinery, entrances, braces, rails, service access and useful machinery. Medium detail that reads at game zoom, with strong large and medium forms; no primitive blocks standing in for buildings, no photorealism, no generic modern human factories, no excessive steampunk brass, no sci-fi neon. No invented heat meters or maintenance systems. All architecture fits its declared footprint; roof, structural supports, working machinery and access decks contained inside the tile boundary. A small beaver silhouette by each entrance establishes scale. Each building sits on a clearly drawn square tile grid with a thin footprint outline, on a calm warm-grey presentation background. Show no roads protruding from the building except a small entrance arrow outside its grid. Title and labels use a simple highly readable compact presentation typeface. A small UI glyph accompanies each building: MONOCHROME warm ivory/gold linework on dark teal, crisp solid strokes, a few solid-filled details and negative space, no colored illustration, no 3D miniature, no gradient; match the simple line-drawn official Timberborn JamStove and BerryJam icon style. These are original new designs, not copies of existing meshes. Top title 'DEEP FRONTIER'; subtitle states 'Concept study — not in-game assets'.
Board: MINING & MATERIAL SOURCES. Wide landscape concept board, three primary building presentations with ample space. Top left: 'Sandstone pit · 2 × 2 · 2 high' — a compact timber-built quarrymen's lodge with an open sorting bay, one small sloping canopy, a bench holding ochre sandstone, manual sorting grating, a small hand winch and crate rack. It is a staffed gathering workplace, not a huge excavator and not a hole in its own foundation. Top right: 'Limestone pit · 2 × 2 · 2 high' — related but distinguishable silhouette, pale limestone bins, sheltered tool store and wheelbarrow loading bay. Lower half dominant hero: 'Permanent mineral quarry · 5 × 5 · 4 high' — substantial post-and-beam extraction headframe bridging a compact dark vertical mine opening WITHIN an entirely flat 5-by-5 foundation; visible bucket hoist, gear-driven winch, ore sorting bin, grated workers' platform, ladders, machinery shelter, water inlet on one side, shaft-power coupling on another. A plausible industrial building, not a gigantic exposed wedge of rock. Include two small ore swatches at its label (ochre sandstone, pale limestone) to communicate shared architecture with mineral-specific material bins. A narrow bottom strip labeled 'Map sources' shows four SMALL geological studies: low jagged ochre sandstone outcrop and pale limestone outcrop each '1 × 1 finite'; flat geological seam markers with fractured soil, subtle strata and exposed ore, each '5 × 5 permanent'. Seam markers are low geological features buildable-over, not five-tile tall mountains. Keep machinery inside the indicated footprint and distinguish base height from tower height. Include small simplified top-view footprint miniatures by the labels, grids 2-by-2, 2-by-2 and 5-by-5. Strong clean visual hierarchy, high quality readable design review board.

Board: CONCRETE PRODUCTION. Wide landscape, THREE equally important large isometric building designs side by side, each with a small top-down grid plan below. The actual grid dimensions and model proportions must agree. LEFT 'Stone crusher · 3 × 3 · 2 high · 200 hp': low broad timber-framed crushing mill occupying most of its nine-tile base, slanted sandstone input hopper, two visible toothed crushing rollers under a substantial protective timber canopy, chunky iron flywheel and native mechanical-shaft socket, aggregate chute and filled output bin within the footprint, beaver door and sorting platform. CENTER 'Cement kiln · 3 × 4 · 3 high · 300 hp': longer rectangular industrial timber kiln-house on twelve tiles, sturdy ash-grey masonry furnace with a dark iron rotary barrel inside an open-sided covered hall, clearly sheltered limestone/dirt hopper at one end, log-fuel bay, narrow stout chimney within three-tile height, restrained warm furnace interior, enclosed cement discharge bin. Make it a legible building, not a loose cylinder. RIGHT 'Concrete mixer · 3 × 3 · 3 high · 250 hp': substantial braced timber mixing house on nine tiles, angled dark iron mixing drum supported on trunnions, a compact raised cement feed bin, aggregate loading hopper, wooden water cask with an iron pipe into the drum, mechanical drive wheel, front discharge chute into a low collection bin, a covered side entrance, small catwalk and guardrails. Each full building should read immediately as a different machine even in silhouette. Under each top-view mini plan, show a tiny curved arrow identifying one intended moving assembly: crusher rollers; kiln barrel; mixer drum. These are animation design notes, not a heat/maintenance mechanic. Bottom concise recipe captions only: 'Sandstone → Aggregate', 'Limestone + Dirt + Logs → Cement', 'Aggregate + Cement + Water → Concrete'. Each building has its own tiny monochrome line-art UI icon. No large landscape, no oversized conveyors crossing the footprint, no palette of colored UI icons.

Board: A LIVING INDUSTRIAL COLONY. Wide landscape 2-by-2 grid of four detailed yet game-scale buildings, each on a true 3-by-3 tile footprint, height no more than three tile units. These are Iron Teeth civic buildings, warm and welcoming while sharing the industrial timber/iron vocabulary. TOP LEFT 'Hospital · 3 × 3 · 3 high': substantial compact two-storey timber clinic with angular roof, broad accessible ground-floor entrance, banded metal structural corners, shuttered ward windows, small sheltered reception porch contained inside its footprint, water tank tucked under rear eaves, modest medicine-bottle carved wooden sign (NO red cross), simple flower box, distinct roof silhouette. TOP RIGHT 'Restaurant · 3 × 3 · 3 high': inviting two-storey workers' dining hall, heavy timber construction, real wide dining-room windows, visible warm kitchen and stout flue, small food serving hatch, compact covered entry with a carved bowl-and-spoon sign; no neon, no sidewalk furniture extending outside grid. BOTTOM LEFT 'Grocery store · 3 × 3 · 3 high': industrial colony cooperative shop, asymmetrical stepped roof, sheltered customer entrance, generous display windows, racks of sacks and food crates inside an open storefront, a receiving door on the side, a small basket sign, all structure and storage inside nine tiles. BOTTOM RIGHT 'Fishery works · 3 × 3 · 3 high': practical timber-and-metal fish processing building, steep short roof and a small vent, sheltered cleaning/sorting area, two compact receiving vats and output crates under the structure, side water inlet, fish-shaped carved sign; clearly a processing workshop rather than an invented huge fish pond. Each design has a beaver-scale doorway, restrained planted or furnished details, highly recognizable silhouette, and its own monochrome linework icon. Human urban buildings and folktail fantasy cottages must be avoided. Show four small 3-by-3 top-view grid diagrams under their labels, with entrances visibly marked. Do not suggest these pictures are finished game assets.

Use case: stylized-concept. Create a clean original UI ICON STYLE REVIEW SHEET for 'DEEP FRONTIER' a Timberborn Iron Teeth mod. Landscape image, dark muted teal background. Subtitle 'Monochrome UI study'. Exactly SIXTEEN icons arranged in a spacious four-column by four-row grid. Each icon is a simple warm ivory/gold MONOCHROME line drawing, some small solid-filled shapes, transparent-looking negative spaces showing the teal background. Match the official Timberborn mod example aesthetic: slightly hand-drawn stout pale outlines, highly simplified readable orthographic/isometric architectural or material symbols, no shaded color, no gradient, no 3D render, no colored square artwork. Icons have consistent stroke weight, equal optical mass, simple silhouettes that would read at 32px. At the bottom of each icon cell show a smaller version at UI button size as a legibility sample. No decorative button borders. Building icons should look like small architectural wireframe/pictogram drawings, with roof shape, entrance and characteristic machinery; resource icons look like stylized outlined goods. Row 1 labels and subjects in order: 'Sandstone pit' a small braced open shelter and rock bin; 'Limestone pit' a short roofed lodge and pale-stone bin, distinct shape; 'Stone crusher' mill with prominent toothed rollers and hopper; 'Cement kiln' compact covered barrel furnace and chimney. Row 2: 'Concrete mixer' braced workshop with angled mixing drum; 'Deep quarry' substantial mining headframe and hoist; 'Hospital' two-storey clinic with bottle sign, no red cross; 'Restaurant' dining hall with bowl sign. Row 3: 'Grocery store' timber shopfront and basket; 'Fishery works' workshop with fish sign; 'Nuclear reactor' compact containment vessel with thick service pipes and small angular shelter; 'Cryogenic plant' paired insulated tanks with a braced compressor shed. Row 4: 'Sandstone' three angular layered stones; 'Aggregate' pile of chunky gravel; 'Cement' plain binder sack with a simple tied neck; 'Concrete' two squat cast blocks. Labels in a small simple cream sans-serif typeface. Pale gold/ivory is the only icon color. Silhouette, stroke discipline and clarity matter more than minute detail. This is concept art for review, not a screenshot, not final sprites. No foreign game logos, no colored ore icons, no realistic materials, no rendered building miniatures.
